data.result:
I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's a complete configuration:

## Server-side setup (run on `server`):

**1. Create a bare git repository:**
```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
git init --bare /git/server
```

**2. Create the web directory and post-receive hook:**
```bash
# Create web root
mkdir -p /var/www/html

# Create the post-receive hook
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/html git checkout -f
EOF

# Make it executable
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

**3. Set up a web server on port 8080:**

Using Python 3 (simplest):
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080 &
```

Or using Node.js with `http-server`:
```bash
npm install -g http-server
cd /var/www/html
http-server -p 8080
```

Or using a persistent systemd service with Python. Create `/etc/systemd/system/webserver.service`:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Simple HTTP Server on port 8080
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/html
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8080
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Then enable it:
```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable webserver.service
sudo systemctl start webserver.service
```

## Client-side usage (on your computer):

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-project
cd my-project
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

**How it works:** When you push, the post-receive hook automatically checks out the latest files from the git repo into `/var/www/html`, making them immediately available via the web server.

## Server-side setup (run on `server`):

**1. Create a bare git repository:**
```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
git init --bare /git/server
```

**2. Create the web directory and post-receive hook:**
```bash
# Create web root
mkdir -p /var/www/html

# Create the post-receive hook
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/html git checkout -f
EOF

# Make it executable
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

**3. Set up a web server on port 8080:**

Using Python 3 (simplest):
```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080 &
```

Or using Node.js with `http-server`:
```bash
npm install -g http-server
cd /var/www/html
http-server -p 8080
```

Or using a persistent systemd service with Python. Create `/etc/systemd/system/webserver.service`:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Simple HTTP Server on port 8080
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/html
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 8080
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Then enable it:
```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable webserver.service
sudo systemctl start webserver.service
```

## Client-side usage (on your computer):

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-project
cd my-project
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

**How it works:** When you push, the post-receive hook automatically checks out the latest files from the git repo into `/var/www/html`, making them immediately available via the web server.
